items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-119096 (score CVSS 9.8).

The Uncanny Toolkit for LearnDash plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass in versions up to, and including, 3.8.2 via the `email` parameter of the `uo_login_action()` function. This is due to a parser-differential flaw in which the plugin's account-verification gate resolves the submitted `email` value using the raw, unsanitized string passed to `get_user_by()`, while the subsequent `wp_signon()` call relies on WordPress core's internal `sanitize_user()` to strip appended junk characters — causing the gate lookup to fail and be skipped entirely while the real account is still resolved and authenticated. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in to unverified or administrator-suspended accounts whose credentials they already possess, obtaining a valid `wordpress_logged_in` session cookie and defeating the plugin's account-approval and account-suspension controls. The nonce required to reach the handler is freely obtainable in the same request from the unauthenticated `ult-refresh-nonce` endpoint, making exploitation trivial for any attacker with network access to the site and knowledge of a target account's credentials.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-287

items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique CVE-2026-109220 (score CVSS 9.8).

The PDF Invoice for WooCommerce + Drag and Drop Template Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.1 via the 'customer_note' parameter parameter. This is due to insufficient sanitization of the customer_note checkout field, which is inlined verbatim into invoice HTML, entity-decoded back into a live tag by simplehtmldom, reassembled into raw bytes by mPDF, and passed to unserialize() in _getObjAttr without validation. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger the vulnerable code path on a default install by placing an anonymous WooCommerce checkout via the public Store API (POST /wc/store/v1/checkout) using a Direct Bank Transfer or cheque payment method, which automatically transitions the order to 'on-hold' status and fires the plugin's invoice-generation hook.

Score CVSS : 9.8

Type de faiblesse (CWE) : CWE-502

items.detail:
Vulnérabilité critique affectant Palo Alto.

Attackers have chained critical PHP2Shell vulnerabilities with the Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw to gain root access on Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS systems.

The campaign reportedly compromised 24 internet-facing firewalls before reaching an internal firewall management server, bringing the total to 25 compromised systems.

Hunt.io’s investigation cites Dream Research’s campaign analysis and describes a transition from honeypot exploitation to production compromises.

However, the findings do not establish reliable mass exploitation across arbitrary PHP servers, where differing software builds and memory layouts complicate successful attacks.

PHP2Shell comprises CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 , two critical memory-safety vulnerabilities rated CVSS 4.0 9.2. The flaws involve PHP session-upload handling and memory cleanup during out-of-memory conditions, potentially enabling remote code execution in vulnerable configurations.

The attack begins through PHP’s session.upload_progress mechanism, which processes attacker-controlled multipart upload data.

Crafted requests manipulate heap allocations, expose memory addresses needed to bypass address space layout randomization, and forge internal structures that redirect execution to PHP’s system() function.

C’est une méthode bien connue des équipes commerciales et des professionnels du marketing. Vous connaissez le nom d’un décideur, son prénom ainsi que l’entreprise dans laquelle il travaille. En observant la syntaxe habituelle des courriels de cette société, par exemple prenom.nom@entreprise.fr , il devient un jeu d’enfant de déduire son adresse directe, même si celle-ci n’a jamais été publiée explicitement sur Internet. Pourtant, comme le souligne la CNIL (Commission Nationale de l’Informatique et des Libertés), le fait qu’une information soit accessible en ligne ne signifie pas qu’elle soit librement exploitable . Reconstituer une adresse électronique professionnelle constitue un traitement de données personnelles à part entière, soumis à des règles strictes. Entre intérêt légitime et respect de la vie privée Pour justifier cette pratique sans avoir à demander un accord préalable, les organismes s’appuient généralement sur la notion d’« intérêt légitime » prévue par le RGPD . Mais la CNIL avertit que ce fondement juridique n’est pas un chèque en blanc. L’entreprise doit impérativement prouver que son besoin de contact est réel et qu’il ne porte pas une atteinte excessive aux droits de l’interlocuteur. Toute la question repose sur ce que le professionnel peut « raisonnablement s’attendre »

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par CISA Advisories.

CISA, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Cyber Centre), and partners are releasing joint guidance, Managing AI Token Consumption for Operational Resilience , to help organizations understand and manage token usage in support of operations. As organizations adopt third-party super intelligence (SI) services, token-based usage models can affect cost, performance, and access to critical services. Unmanaged token consumption may contribute to rising and unpredictable costs, reduced service availability, degraded performance, token exhaustion, and denial-of-tokens or denial-of-wallet attacks. The guidance outlines practical steps organizations can take to prioritize token allocation, design efficient workflows, improve user prompting practices, leverage caching and reusable context, optimize data before submission, and monitor token consumption over time. Critical infrastructure owners and operators can use this guidance to identify mission-critical functions that depend on SI, understand service provider and operational dependencies, and plan for reduced SI availability during outages, incidents, or periods of high demand. “An unauthorized party gained access to a system or database containing company or customer information,” the department said in a statement. “FLDOE is partnering with the Florida Digital Service and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement in its response to the event.”

FLDOE has taken the financial aid site down and warned that other department websites and services may experience temporary disruptions. Financial aid for students is not at risk and the breach will not delay aid disbursements or tuition payments. The incident will also not impact scholarships, grants or student loans.

The state urged those affected to monitor their credit reports and financial accounts for any irregular activity.

This story is interesting: One Civic owner purchased a cheap aftermarket head unit off Amazon, and decided to have Claude work its magic on it, like it would a smart TV. What was reportedly discovered isn’t surprising, but is worth knowing about. Among the pre-installed bloatware—­or spyware, if you’re being less charitable­—was a voice assistant equipped with WebView, an Android system component that lets apps display content off the web. This apparently always used about a third of processing power, even while idle, which isn’t great. There were also Baidu location services, a call recorder (!), a DAB radio client that is pretty much useless in the U.S., and Adobe Acrobat, presumably so your passenger can entertain themselves with PDFs on the go. It’s interesting because it exposes all the insecurities in this piece of IoT software. But I think the real story is that a random person was able to do this reverse-engineering with the help of AI. Expect a lot more stories like this in the future.

items.detail:
Incident de sécurité rapporté par Infosecurity Mag.

France-based operators of Danfoss refrigeration controllers have sharply reduced their internet exposure after the October 11 cyber-attack

Internet-exposed refrigeration controllers in France are disappearing from public view at a dramatic rate following a cyber incident targeting supermarket food supplies .

Censys researchers observed a 71% drop in internet-exposed Danfoss StoreView controllers in just three days after the October 11 cyber-attack targeting hundreds of supermarkets in France, suggesting that operators are moving quickly to limit their systems' online exposure.

Danfoss StoreView was among the equipment targeted by this cyber-attack . StoreView instances are typically used as control panels for Danfoss refrigeration controllers that are installed in many French supermarket fridges and freezers.

Danfoss, a Danish temperature regulation systems provider, has confirmed its equipment was targeted by the cyber-attack, and said most affected controllers were either older models that no longer received security updates (AK-SM800 and AK-SC355) or newer models running outdated firmware (AK-SM800A).

Danfoss patched three vulnerabilities in its AK-SM 800A controllers in March 2025 (CVE-2025-41450) and August 2025 (CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452).

A year later, a researcher at industrial security provider Claroty demonstrated how CVE-2025-41450 and CVE-2025-41451 could be chained together to achieve remote code execution and thus disable cooling while falsifying temperature readings, potentially concealing failures in the cold chain.

Jusqu’où pourra-t-on repousser les limites physiques du stockage ? La deeptech française Biomemory , issue des travaux de recherche de Sorbonne Université et du CNRS, franchit un cap avec le lancement de DNA Shield. Présenté comme son premier produit commercial fondé sur sa plateforme d’« informatique moléculaire », il s’agit d’un service géré de conservation hors ligne de données critiques, encodées dans de l’ADN synthétique. DNA Shield vise les informations dont une organisation souhaite préserver l’intégrité sur le long terme : les clés cryptographiques, la propriété intellectuelle, les registres réglementés ou encore archives institutionnelles. Les données sont d’abord sélectionnées et chiffrées par le client, puis encodées dans de l’ADN synthétique conservé hors ligne, sous garde gérée. La récupération n’est pas conçue comme un accès permanent ou en libre-service. Biomemory décrit un processus contrôlé et déclenché lorsque cela s’avère nécessaire. L’ECSC est la compétition annuelle qui oppose les équipes nationales européennes sur des épreuves pratiques de type Capture the Flag ( CTF )*.

L’édition 2026 réunit 35 pays européens et sept nations invitées : l’Arménie, l’Australie, le Canada, le Costa Rica, le Kosovo, Singapour et les États-Unis.

Jeopardy : les équipes résolvent des défis en sécurité web, cryptographie, rétro-ingénierie ou exploitation de vulnérabilités logicielles et matérielles. Chaque défi résolu livre un « flag » qui rapporte des points, et moins un défi est résolu par les concurrents, plus il vaut cher.

The company, billing itself as “the next-generation fashion retailer for Millennial and Generation Z consumers,” said a recent hack exposed customer payment card numbers.

Online fashion retailer Revolve warned investors that cybercriminals gained access to payment card numbers and expiration dates during a recent cyber incident.

The clothing giant filed an 8-K report on Thursday with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) saying hackers gained access to multiple company systems.

Revolve did not respond to questions about when the attack occurred but said in the report that an initial investigation found that the threat actors used “automated means” to obtain names, contact information, payment card numbers and payment card expiration dates from customers who saved payment information in their online shopping account on Revolve’s e-commerce platform.

Revolve said it has notified federal law enforcement agencies about the attack and has hired a cybersecurity firm to lead the recovery effort. There were no operational disruptions caused by the attack, and Revolve said it will not face material financial impacts as a result of the incident.

The company, which bills itself as “the next-generation fashion retailer for Millennial and Generation Z consumers,” did not say how many people were affected but told regulators in Texas on Friday that 127,200 people in the state had information stolen. items.detail:
Signal de veille — The Register.

General Motors is taking what looks like a light slap on the wrist from a coalition of 35 states and the District of Columbia after agreeing to settle allegations that it collected drivers' data without proper consent and sold it to data brokers that supplied insurance companies. The Washington state AG's office said on Thursday that GM had reached a $220 million settlement with 36 attorneys general over the automaker's collection and sharing of driving data, including precise location information, speed, seatbelt use, and other metrics. According to investigators, GM sold that data to brokers, which in turn supplied it to insurance companies that could use it to set customers' premiums, without drivers' informed consent. For reference, the $220 million settlement, which will be distributed among the participating jurisdictions, equates to less than 7 percent of GM's $3.3 billion in net income attributable to stockholders for its third quarter, which ended on September 30, 2026. Don't spend it all in one place, y'all. The settlement comes more than two years after a 2024 New York Times investigation found that GM had been selling the data collected from vehicle owners through its Smart Driver program. That program, part of GM subsidiary OnStar’s offering, collected the aforementioned data and handed it back to vehicle owners in reports designed to inform better driving habits.
